title: Reducing Migrant Domestic Workers' Upfront Costs for Families with Young Children or Vulnerable Elderly and Enhancing Employer Protections
what_it_is: Reducing Migrant Domestic Workers' Upfront Costs for Families with Young Children or Vulnerable Elderly and Enhancing Employer Protections

sections.label: Migrant domestic worker hiring costs
sections.summary: MP asks whether MOM plans to reduce upfront MDW hiring costs and strengthen protections against agency misrepresentation and MDW offences or early cessation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry has any plans to (i) further reduce upfront costs to hire migrant domestic workers (MDW) for families with young children or vulnerable elderly and (ii) enhance protections against misrepresentation from agencies, and MDWs who commit offences or wish to cease work for reasons not due to employer fault, such as homesickness; and (b) if so, what are these plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This upfront cost has remained largely stable since 2022, after accounting for inflation.

sections.label: MDW refunds, levies, offence bars
sections.summary: MOM requires employment agencies to refund at least 50% of service fees if an MDW's contract ends within six months without replacement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: When there is a mismatch of MDWs with employers, MOM requires EAs to refund employers at least 50% of the service fees paid if MDW's contract is terminated within the first six months of employment without a suitable replacement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Families with young children and elderly enjoy significant subsidies today in the form of concessionary levies at about $60 a month instead of $300.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This amounts to about $5,760 in savings over two years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: MDWs who commit serious offences, such as stealing, are barred from future employment in Singapore.

sections.label: Agency fee benchmarks question
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it would set benchmark ranges for agency fees, but says service fees are generally left to market forces.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider establishing benchmark ranges for agency fees based on prevailing market practices to prevent excessive charges and ensure affordability for families?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: We generally allow agency service fees to be determined by market forces.

sections.label: Caregiving Grant increase
sections.summary: The Caregiving Grant provides about $400 and will be increased in April 2026 to $600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: For example, the Caregiving Grant, which provides about $400 of payout, and this will be increased in April 2026 to $600.

sections.label: Household Services Scheme cleaning option
sections.summary: Families without caregiving needs can consider part-time cleaning services under the Household Services Scheme, which may be more affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
sentences.text: For families without caregiving needs, they also can consider part time cleaning services under the Household Services Scheme, which may be more affordable.
